patterns.what_worked: Re-pointing the class wrappers at the class's own drill (the class module publishes PRACTICE_DRILL_KEY + practice_drill_key(); the session keeps the harness's shared primitives as its state and grades through the class's own drill function) made the retired built-in's truth provably dead: the mutation proofs (7/7 killed) show a wrapper that still starts the built-in, or that grades with the retired rule, or that carries the namespace alias, all fail a pin.
patterns.what_was_hard: The engine reads ONE accessor for two different things (the retired built-in's routing key and the scenario id), so the class cannot rename practice_scenario_key without arming the engine's fail-closed 'drill route broken' path - the key therefore stays the built-in and the class's own drill is published through a new accessor. The shaman module sits exactly on Lua 5.1's 200-local limit, so the new helpers had to be inlined. The shaman's own drill needs the decision engine loaded, so the class suite now loads shaman_guide.lua.
patterns.skill_gap: Deciding, without the engine lane's file, where the mastery row's drill id lives: the panel map (PRACTICE_DRILL_KEYS.*.mode) still names the class's first drill while the wrappers run the superseding drill - filed for the engine lane with the exact one-line change per class.
